Hello,

I have a Mitsubishi Laser (from De Freitas) and have acquired the appropriate housing. However, I am not able to focus the beam in a spot. I have adjusted the position of the lens by turning it in the housing. I can change the spreading of the beam but I can't reduce it to a nice little spot. ( At a distance of 1 m, I'll become a spot of ca. 10 cm.

Is somebody familiar with this problem? What can I do?

Pascal

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
Form your figures, I suspect it's a negative lens. I'd thought it might be a positive lens with an extremely short focal length, but the 6 degree beam spread seems to make that possibility unlikely. If it is a negative lens, it won't focus light to a real point, but expands the beam. There's a virtual focus behind the lens. To focus it, you need another , positive lens. 

To find the appropriate lens to focus at a particular point, use the lens formula:

1/u + 1/v = 1/f

u = distance of laser from lens

v=distance of focused point from lens

f = focal length of lens

and the fact that the beam spread seems to be about 6 degrees, which will give you the necessary diameter(d) for the required lens as:

d = (2*v)*tan(3)

So if you want to focus the beam at 80 cm and you choose to put the lens at 20 cm, then u=20, v=60 and, using the lens formula, you need a lens of focal length

 f= 1/( 1/20 + 1/60) = 15cm. 

The diameter of the lens will be

d = 2*60*tan(3) = 6cm

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: I'm just guessing, but maybe if the lens is plano convex the orientation (flat side facing diode versus the reverse) matters for focusing. Try flipping it over and see if it works better. I don't know what the proper orientation should be... - most likely flat side facing diode.

posts.author: Pascal
posts.content_md:
I've tried changing the side of the lens and it isn't working.

I've bought a standard component (housing with lens) recommended by De Freitas and it simply doesn't work properly. (The diode fits nicely in the housing, so it looks good) So I am wondering, what could I have done wrong???

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Is the problem that you can't get the lens close enough to the diode to collimate it? It should work, and if not I suggest you look closely at how the barrel is threaded and the diode mounting arrangement and try to figure out what is preventing you from getting the lens close enough.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: Maybe the diode is too close. If the point of divergence of the laser is inside the focal length of the lens, ie the "object distance" is less than the focal length of the lens, then the positive lens would act as a diverging lens, since the "image point" is now virtual.

It should work, and if not I suggest you look closely at how the barrel is threaded and the diode mounting arrangement and try to figure out what is preventing you from getting the lens close enough.

I have had this problem with this housing. The diode is not seated all of the way. Gently seat the diode all the way to the stop.
